<description>
Changes making it possible to call `interface::Chain` over a socket.

Note: The changes in this PR allow a `bitcoin-node` process to be controlled over a socket. The socket can either be an UNIX socket created by specifying the `-ipcbind` option, or it can be a socketpair created by a controlling process and passed to `bitcoin-node` via the `-ipcfd=<n>` with a file descriptor number. This PR is a dependency of #10102 which allows the wallet code to run in a separate process and use the `Chain` interface.

---

This PR is part of the [process separation project](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/28722).

**This is based on https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/370.** The non-base commits are:

- [`da6e359a004` build: suppress -Wc++23-lambda-attributes in warn_interface](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409/commits/da6e359a0041fccd925ff32ad1e1ec5e7dc89782)
- [`dbded7d5e86` Add capnp serialization code for bitcoin types](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409/commits/dbded7d5e86bb0a4f19f25fbe7e2ce38e6dfa80f)
- [`b47545b94a3` Add capnp wrapper for Handler interface](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409/commits/b47545b94a30e67e17b9bd46e1959801880ca93d)
- [`2ee7fc45cf3` Add capnp wrapper for Chain interface](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409/commits/2ee7fc45cf3658b954bff017db45024b2a37a0ba)
- [`8801a9cb135` multiprocess: Expose Chain interface](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409/commits/8801a9cb1356a20ad6f39041cadfae1bea80f16c)
</description>

[2026-10-14] rc:4267760541 inline on src/ipc/capnp/chain.capnp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-10-14):
re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409#discussion_r4190833185

Thanks for the clear report and the test. #36520 fixes this by catching `ipc::Exception` errors from notification handlers in `NotificationsProxy` and logging them, so they no longer escape the scheduler thread. Exceptions from in-process handlers like the wallet are still not caught, since those indicate bugs.

It doesn't drop the handler after an error. If the client disconnects, the handler it registered is destroyed along with the connection, and a client that returns an error from one notification may still want the others. Could revisit if that turns out to be a problem in practice.

[2026-10-14] rc:4267761617 inline on src/rpc/request.h by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-10-14):
re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409#discussion_r4185159458

I think this one is still accurate: `JSONRPCRequest` in `chain.capnp` has a field for each member of this struct except `context`, which can't be sent over IPC. Did you see something out of sync? There was a similar note in `block_policy_estimator.h` that was stale, and I removed it in the latest push along with the unused fee estimation structs.
[2026-10-14] rc:4267761744 inline on src/ipc/capnp/chain.capnp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-10-14):
re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409#discussion_r4185638717

I think it's simpler to leave this as is. The size and fee values come from the same mempool lookup as the counts, so always returning them only costs two extra integers in the response. `FoundBlock` has want-flags because some of its fields, like block data, are expensive to read and large to send, which isn't the case here.
[2026-10-14] rc:4267761935 inline on src/ipc/capnp/chain.capnp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-10-14):
re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409#discussion_r4185693340

`metadata_fn` is a function pointer, so it can't be sent over IPC. Right now nothing in this PR needs it, but you're pointing at a real gap: `getopenrpcinfo` skips commands without `metadata_fn`, so wallet RPCs would be missing from it once the wallet runs in a separate process in #10102. Fixing that would mean sending the method description as data instead of a function pointer. I'll look at it as part of #10102.
[2026-10-14] rc:4267762086 inline on src/ipc/capnp/chain.capnp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-10-14):
re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409#discussion_r4205046814

Agree this would be useful, and the C++ side already has a place for it: `Chain::NotifyOptions::connect_undo_data`. #24230 adds an `attachChain` method that takes these options and reads undo data for clients that ask for it (it's what the indexes use). Once that's in, exposing it over IPC should be simple.

On the format, I agree serialized `CBlockUndo` isn't very convenient for non-C++ clients. Sending a list of spent coins would be friendlier, and could be done in the capnp layer without changing the C++ interface. I'd prefer to leave both for a follow-up, since this PR is just trying to wrap the existing interface.
[2026-10-14] rc:4267762259 inline on src/ipc/capnp/chain.capnp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-10-14):
re: darosior https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409#discussion_r1871523229

Sorry for missing this. The capnp method mirrors the existing C++ `Chain::Notifications::updatedBlockTip()` method, which also takes no arguments. The wallet uses it as a signal to check the tip again and doesn't need details pushed to it. It could take arguments in the future if a client needs them, but this PR just wraps the interface as it is.
[2026-10-14] rc:4267762443 inline on src/ipc/capnp/chain.capnp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-10-14):
re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29409#discussion_r1876772189

Sorry for missing this. `CAmount` is an `int64_t` typedef, so it maps directly to `Int64`. `CFeeRate` is a class with serialization methods, so it goes through the generic code in `common-types.h` that sends serializable objects as `Data`, the same as transactions and other types. It wasn't a deliberate choice for fee rates, and a struct would be friendlier for non-C++ clients, so that could be a good follow-up.
